findings.title: Team admin check uses `&&` instead of `||`
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. In Cal.com's team membership model a user's role is either `ADMIN` or `OWNER`, not both, depending on how `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` are implemented (`isTeamOwner` requires `role: 'OWNER'`). Using `&&` instead of `||` means a team admin who is not the team owner (and not the booking organizer or attendee) will be denied permission with `FORBIDDEN` when trying to add guests to a team booking.

findings.title: Calendar update uses caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials
findings.body: `addGuestsHandler` allows an attendee or a team admin/owner to add guests to a booking (`isTeamAdminOrOwner || isOrganizer || isAttendee`), but then fetches credentials with `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and constructs `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` using the logged-in caller (`ctx.user`) rather than `booking.user` (the organizer). When an attendee or a team admin who is not the organizer adds guests, `EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` will try to update the calendar event using the caller's credentials and calendar integrations instead of the organizer's, so the organizer's external calendar invite (Google/Office365, etc.) will not be updated with the new attendees.

findings.title: Duplicate emails in `input.guests` and case-insensitive duplicates are not deduplicated on the server
findings.body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `z.array(z.string().email())` without enforcing uniqueness, and `uniqueGuests` in `addGuestsHandler` only filters against existing `booking.attendees` (with case-sensitive `===`) and `blacklistedGuestEmails` (which is lowercased while `guest` is not). If a client calls the tRPC endpoint with duplicate emails in `guests`, or with an email that differs only in casing from an existing attendee or blacklisted address, duplicate attendee rows will be created in the database and blacklisted guests can bypass the blacklist when uppercase characters are used.

findings.title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores `disableStandardEmails` eventType metadata settings
findings.body: Other email sender functions in `packages/emails/email-manager.ts` (such as `sendLocationChangeEmails`, `sendScheduledEmails`, `sendRescheduledEmails`) accept `eventTypeMetadata` and check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` before sending emails to hosts or attendees. `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not check these flags at all, so bookings on event types configured to suppress standard host or attendee emails will still send emails to the organizer, team members, and all attendees when guests are added.

findings.title: "Additional Guests" action is shown for past bookings
findings.body: `editBookingActions` (which now includes `add_members`) is rendered via `bookedActions` even when `isBookingInPast` is true (lines 553-554: `isBookingInPast && isConfirmed ? <TableActions actions={bookedActions} /> : null`), and `addGuestsHandler` does not check whether the booking has already ended. Users can therefore add guests to past bookings, which triggers calendar updates and sends "Guests Added" / "New event scheduled" invitation emails for meetings that have already taken place.

findings.title: `isInvalidEmail` error banner is not cleared on successful submission or when reopening the dialog
findings.body: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when validation fails, and is only reset to `false` in the Cancel button's `onClick`. It is not reset when the user edits the email fields, when `addGuestsMutation` succeeds, or when the dialog is closed via the backdrop / Escape key (`onOpenChange`). If a user triggers a validation error once and then fixes the email and submits (or closes the dialog via Escape and reopens it), the red error message remains visible.
